articles.title: Utah man spent at least $367,599 on an Airstream trailer, a BMW and jewellery during divorce; appeals court sends marital asset dispute back for review
articles.summary: A Utah man was found to have spent at least $367,599 during his divorce on purchases including an Airstream trailer, a BMW for one daughter and jewellery
articles.body: A Utah man was found to have spent at least $367,599 during his divorce on purchases including an Airstream trailer, a BMW for one daughter and jewellery for his daughters. The district court found that Brandon Reynolds Bonham had violated court orders by spending marital money without his wife's consent.It also found that he had failed to disclose expenditures and provide an account of the money used. The court ordered him to pay his former wife 75% of the amount found dissipated, but the appeals court reversed that award. According to the Utah Court of Appeals' judgment in Bonham v. Bonham, the lower court must reassess dissipation and award Emily half of the total established.Brandon Bonham spent marital money during divorce proceedingsEmily and Brandon Bonham married in July 1998 and separated in July 2019 after Brandon admitted to an extramarital affair that resulted in the birth of a child. Emily petitioned for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences and the affair. They had four children together, three of whom were minors when she filed.The couple also had a large marital estate, including a home and RMT Equipment, a business that Brandon continued to operate during the proceedings. Under temporary orders, he was required to pay Emily monthly family support and salary through RMT, cover vehicle and health insurance costs, and share the cost of the children's existing extracurricular activities. The divorce trial took place over four days in August and September 2022.Court found at least $367,599 in marital asset dissipationThe district court said the parties were subject to a rule preventing either from disposing of marital property without the other's consent. Its temporary order also prohibited them from dissipating or liquidating marital assets. The court found that Brandon had intentionally breached those restrictions on multiple occasions. It said he spent thousands of dollars on toys, gifts, holidays and other purchases during the litigation.According to the findings, he disclosed the purchases after Emily discovered them and did not provide a full accounting of the marital money used. The court identified at least $367,599 in dissipation, while stating that the total was likely higher. Listed expenditures included an Airstream trailer, a BMW for a daughter and jewellery for the daughters.Brandon challenges 75% marital asset dissipation awardThe district court held Brandon in contempt and imposed a sanction under Utah law. Rather than awarding Emily half of the amount found to have been dissipated, it ordered Brandon to pay her 75%. The court said the higher share reflected his repeated violations of the injunction and temporary orders, as well as his failure to disclose enough information to assess the marital estate and identify purchases made with marital funds. In a post-trial motion, Brandon argued he had disclosed much of the spending, including the Airstream and a dirt bike. He also disputed other parts of the divorce decree, including property valuations, alimony, support arrears and attorney fees.Appeals court orders fresh review of marital assets and alimonyThe Utah Court of Appeals affirmed parts of the divorce decree but reversed others and sent several issues back to the district court. On marital asset dissipation, it reversed the 75% award and directed the lower court to make adequate findings about what dissipation had occurred. Emily was to receive half of the total established. The appeals court also reversed the award of equity in the Rolling Brook house, ordering the district court to decide whether it was marital or Brandon's separate property. It required further findings on Brandon's reasonable monthly expenses and tax rate when calculating his ability to pay alimony. The court also ordered revisions to support arrears and further assessment of both initial and post-trial attorney fees.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available court records. The Times of India has not independently verified the expenditures, allegations of marital asset dissipation, court findings or claims made by either party. The findings and rulings are subject to further review by the lower court as directed by the Utah Court of Appeals.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bengaluru family massacre: Man kills wife, mother-in-law, two brothers-in-law, two sisters-in-law and 7-year-old nephew
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Seven members of a family were allegedly murdered in Bengaluru's Srirampura locality, with police suspecting that a prolonged domestic dispute
articles.body: BENGALURU: Seven members of a family were allegedly murdered in Bengaluru's Srirampura locality, with police suspecting that a prolonged domestic dispute may have led to the killings.The accused, identified as Indushekar, allegedly killed his wife and six members of her family, police said on Friday.The victims have been identified as his wife, Sunita; his mother-in-law, Roopavati; his two brothers-in-law, Shivakumar and Shankar; their wives, both named Divya; and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth.Police have so far recovered Puneeth's body.Also read: 'A party invitation': How B'luru family was massacred inside house on 59th CrossThe remaining bodies are suspected to have been dumped at different locations in Bengaluru and neighbouring areas, including Chikkaballapur district.The couple had been married for about 20 years and frequently argued over Sunita's visits to her parental home, according to preliminary findings.Attempts by family members to reconcile the couple failed to resolve their differences. Indushekar allegedly resented the support Sunita received from her mother and brothers and decided to target her family.The killings took place at the accused's house in a residential neighbourhood on 59th Cross, near Bahsyam Circle, within the jurisdiction of Rajajinagar police station.According to preliminary findings, Indushekar allegedly bludgeoned the victims to death with a grinding stone before disposing of their bodies at different locations.He first allegedly killed Sunita with a grinding stone, wrapped her body in cloth and dumped it near Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur district.He then switched off her mobile phone and told neighbours that she had gone on a trip, allegedly in an attempt to avoid suspicion.The following day, Indushekar allegedly invited his brothers-in-law, Shivakumar and Shankar, to his house for a party, where he killed them using the grinding stone.He subsequently allegedly killed their wives, both named Divya, his mother-in-law, Roopavati, and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth, police sources said.Further details about the sequence of events and efforts to recover the remaining bodies are awaited.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Midterm losses, no exits: Marco Rubio rules out quitting, Donald Trump backs Pete Hegseth
articles.summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio has dismissed reports that he is considering leaving the Trump administration following the Republican Party's setbacks
articles.body: US secretary of state Marco Rubio has dismissed reports that he is considering leaving the Trump administration following the Republican Party's setbacks in the midterm elections, saying that completing President Donald Trump's second term has “always been my plan”.In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio rejected speculation that he might step down ahead of a possible 2028 presidential campaign and declined to discuss his political ambitions.“Working for President Trump until the end of his term has always been my plan,” Rubio said, adding that he did not know where reports about his possible departure had originated.“I love the work I’m doing,” he said. “And plus I always laugh when they say he’s going to leave his job. I go, ‘Which one?’”Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, refused to entertain questions about whether he was considering a presidential run in 2028.“I literally will not talk about 2028 anymore,” he told the newspaper in his White House office. “I just won’t do it.”Rubio backs JD Vance for 2028 presidential raceRubio has previously indicated that he would support Vice President JD Vance if he decided to run for president in 2028.“JD is a very good friend of mine,” Rubio told NBC News in May. “If JD runs for president, I think he’d be a phenomenal candidate. I’ve said publicly, and I’ll say it again, I’ll be the first person to sign up and support him.”However, Vance's post-election assessment on Wednesday included criticism of the administration's approach to the Iran war, its policy on Israel and its messaging on the economy.The vice-president blamed the war with Iran for the Republicans' election setbacks and said voters had turned against the administration's position on Israel and its handling of economic concerns. Trump has closely aligned himself with Israel and dismissed concerns over affordability as a “hoax”.Asked whether he agreed with Vance's assessment, Rubio initially deflected, saying he was not “really involved in domestic politics”.However, Rubio acknowledged the political implications of the Iran war when he appeared alongside Trump at a rally in Kansas on Sunday. Trump praised the secretary of state and joked that he might have to fire him because he had become “too popular”.Explaining his presence at the rally, Rubio said he was travelling with the president as the designated national security official. He also acknowledged Trump's remarks that the war had been a factor in the election results.“Higher prices at the gas pump, I acknowledge, is not like the kind of thing you campaign on and brag about,” Rubio said.However, he defended Trump's decision to take action despite its potential political costs, saying the president “deserves a tremendous amount of credit” for doing what he considered necessary.“Ultimately, that is the price of leadership — is the willingness to do things that may not be politically popular or expedient but are necessary for your country and its long-term future,” he said.White House rejects reports of Rubio's possible exitThe White House and the State Department have also rejected reports that Rubio could leave his position following the Republican setbacks.White House spokesperson Beni Rae Harmony described the reports as a fabricated hoax circulated by anonymous sources, while assistant secretary of state for global public affairs Dylan Johnson called them baseless fake news.The speculation over a possible administration shake-up has also involved defence secretary Pete Hegseth, whose handling of the Iran war has drawn criticism following the election losses.The White House has denied reports that Hegseth and Rubio might leave their positions. Trump told ABC News that he had received calls about Hegseth but had “every intention” of keeping him. He later praised the defence secretary, saying he had “done a fantastic job”.However, Republican Representative Thomas Massie has said he intends to move ahead with an effort to impeach Hegseth, with a resolution expected as early as next week. Hegseth has rejected the effort, describing it as a politically motivated attempt to undermine him.Separately, The Washington Post reported that Trump could be considering replacing General Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command.Both have played significant roles in providing guidance on the Iran war.You use AI every day. articles.body: Jyot Singh has made history in the US midterm elections by becoming the first Sikh to be elected to the Georgia House of Representatives.Singh, a Democrat and Yale University alumnus, won the election to represent Georgia House District 97 in the November 3 polls, becoming the first Sikh and Indian-American to serve in the state's General Assembly.Singh secured 13,820 votes, accounting for 68 per cent of the total, defeating his Republican rival Yassin Moghazy, who received 6,509 votes, or 32 per cent.“We made history for our community here in House District 97,” Singh said in a video posted on X following his victory.In his vision statement ahead of the election, Singh highlighted the diversity of Gwinnett County, where he grew up, and spoke about the need to address challenges related to healthcare and housing.“Growing up in Norcross, Georgia, I learned that our diversity isn't just a number—it's our strength. It’s the intricate fabric of Gwinnett, a complex and colourful design where every stitch matters….But I also know that for a tapestry to stay strong, every thread must be secure. I’ve seen the gaps where families fall through—where healthcare is a luxury and housing costs threaten the very roots people have worked so hard to plant.”He said his collective mission was to protect the “excellence we’ve built while ensuring that everyone has the opportunity to bloom.”Singh had earlier defeated Jacques Laurent in the Democratic primary for Georgia House District 97 in May.He holds a high school diploma from the Gwinnett School of Mathematics, Science, and Technology and a bachelor's degree from Yale University. articles.title: A burger van chef inherited a £5 million fortune from a businessman who treated him like a son; the millionaire's sister challenged his will
articles.summary: A burger van chef inherited a £5 million fortune from a businessman who treated him like a son, following a High Court battle with the millionaire's
articles.body: A burger van chef inherited a £5 million fortune from a businessman who treated him like a son, following a High Court battle with the millionaire's estranged sister over his will. Sam Jones secured the inheritance from his late friend David Turner, who died aged 71 in 2017. Despite the life-changing payout, Jones continued working at his burger van in Chertsey, Surrey. The legal dispute centred on Turner's missing original will, with his sister Linda Cano challenging its validity in an attempt to inherit his estate. However, the High Court ruled in Jones's favour, allowing him to retain the fortune, which included a family farm and a share in valuable land near the M25 motorway.Why did the millionaire consider the burger van chef part of his familyAccording to the Sun, Jones and Turner first became friends in 2000 after meeting at a snack bar in Chertsey. Turner, who operated a skip hire business and a family pig farm called Woodside Farm, gradually developed a close relationship with Jones. Their friendship grew through shared interests, including guitars and classic cars, and Turner eventually came to regard him as a member of his family.During the High Court proceedings, Jones's barrister, Rose Fetherstonhaugh, explained the nature of their relationship. She told the hearing: "Mr Turner, who had no children of his own, treated Mr Jones like a son and was very close to his family." She also said that Jones viewed Turner as a father figure, while the businessman had become a grandfather figure to Jones's children. According to the barrister, Jones also cared for Turner during the final months of his life, when his illness had become debilitating.Why did Linda Cano challenge Turner's missing 2013 will in the High CourtTurner's 2013 will became the subject of a legal challenge after his death because the original document could not be found. His estranged sister, Linda Cano, who lived in Spain, questioned whether the will should be accepted without the original testament. Her legal representatives argued that there was no proof Turner had not destroyed the document after changing his mind about who should inherit his estate.Cano sought to have the 2013 will declared invalid, which would have allowed her to inherit under the laws of intestacy. She also told the court that her brother had a history of making and changing his will. However, she accepted that she had had little contact with Turner since 2008. The dispute also involved the brothers and sisters' reportedly strained relationship, with the court hearing that Turner had described his sister in strongly negative terms and had excluded her from his will.Judge rules in the legal battle over the millionaire's missing willMaster Matthew Marsh ruled against Cano and upheld the 2013 will, allowing Jones to inherit Turner's fortune. The judge found that her argument about Turner potentially destroying the original will was not supported by the evidence presented during the proceedings. The court also heard evidence about Jones's regular visits to the farm and his involvement in caring for Turner as his health deteriorated.In his ruling, Master Marsh stated: "There is clear, unchallenged evidence that Mr Jones was a daily visitor to the farm." He also noted that Jones and other people had helped care for Turner during his final illness. The judge added: "There is no evidence that Mr Turner attempted to make a new will." The decision meant that the 2013 testament remained effective and Jones retained his right to inherit the estate.What properties and assets were included in Turner's £5 million inheritanceThe inheritance included Woodside Farm in Chertsey, Surrey, as well as half a share in a valuable plot of land close to the M25 motorway. Turner had operated the farm alongside his skip hire business. The estate also included other bequests to friends, including musical instruments. A donation of £5,000 was left to the British Polio Fellowship, reflecting Turner's experience of having suffered from polio as a child.Despite receiving the fortune, Jones continued to be associated with his burger van business in Chertsey town centre. The Sun reported that the van, named Saffron's Right Food, displayed the slogan "Keeping up with the Joneses" and continued serving customers. Jones was also seen beside the stall while staff worked. The report noted that he maintained a relatively low profile following the court ruling, appearing in casual clothing while the burger van continued operating.You use AI every day. articles.title: More migrants in ICE custody, fewer safety checks: US watchdog warns of oversight gaps
articles.summary: Two watchdog offices tasked with monitoring the treatment of detainees have scaled back their inspections, raising concerns about gaps in accountability
articles.body: Two watchdog offices tasked with monitoring the treatment of detainees have scaled back their inspections, raising concerns about gaps in accountability and the risk of inhumane conditions going unchecked.A new report by the government accountability office (GAO), Congress' investigative watchdog, has warned that fewer inspections could undermine efforts to ensure the safety and humane treatment of people held by US immigration and customs enforcement (ICE).The findings come as the average daily number of people in immigration detention has increased by more than 50% under President Donald Trump, with ICE opening more than 40 additional detention facilities as part of its expansion drive.Inspections nearly halved as detention numbers surgeICE's office of detention oversight (ODO) conducted 194 inspections in 2024, but the number fell to 102 in 2025. The agency's office of the immigration detention ombudsman has also stopped conducting inspections entirely since January after losing its dedicated funding in the 2026 fiscal year.The decline in oversight comes against a sharp rise in the number of people held in ICE custody. The agency detained fewer than 40,000 people at the end of former President Joe Biden's administration. The figure crossed 70,000 in February, following an immigration enforcement surge in Minnesota, and remained above 65,000 as of July.ICE has added more than 40 detention centres since Trump ordered an expansion of its detention capacity early in his second term. Many of these facilities operate out of rented spaces provided by private contractors or state and local governments.Fewer watchdogs, greater risk of unchecked abuseThe GAO warned that the reduction in inspections meant fewer independent checks on whether detention facilities were complying with ICE's own standards. The agency cautioned that the changes could make it harder to identify poor conditions and ensure detainees are treated humanely."These changes may pose risks to ICE ensuring humane detention conditions, as its own guidance calls for," the report said.ICE officials argued that some inspections were duplicative and that the agency could manage without them. However, the GAO said ICE had not provided evidence to support the claim that the inspections were unnecessary.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: As $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq in one day, Nvidia and other technology companies that were the biggest losers
articles.summary: The Nasdaq 100 index erased $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day as Nvidia and other major technology companies suffered steep losses amid
articles.body: The Nasdaq 100 index erased $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day as Nvidia and other major technology companies suffered steep losses amid growing fears over the future of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending in the US. According to a Reuters report, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5% on November 5, marking its biggest one-day drop since the market sell-off triggered by US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025. The sharp decline came after Democrats scored major victories in the US midterm elections, raising concerns that increased political scrutiny and opposition to data centre construction could slow the expansion of AI infrastructure.Nvidia, AMD and semiconductor stocks suffer major lossesNvidia shares dropped 9% during Thursday’s trading session, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) plunged 17%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks major chipmakers, fell 12% and touched its lowest level in more than six months.Several companies directly exposed to AI data centre construction also recorded steep losses. CoreWeave shares fell 10%, while Nebius dropped 15%. Both companies have faced investor concerns over their reliance on borrowing and large-scale infrastructure investments.Data centre operators Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN each tumbled more than 14%. The weakness also extended to companies supplying power and equipment for the AI infrastructure boom. GE Vernova shares fell 7.4%, while Constellation Energy declined 2.5%. Microsoft shares dropped 3.6%, while Amazon and Alphabet each fell 2.2%.Why are investors worried about AI data centresAs stated in the Reuters report, the Democrats’ strong performance in the US midterm elections has raised concerns that local opposition and tighter scrutiny could slow the construction of new data centres. Several incoming Democratic governors, including in Texas, have called for an immediate moratorium on data centre development.Data centres require large amounts of electricity and water, raising concerns among communities about pressure on power grids and local resources. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses.The latest market downturn also comes as investors question whether the enormous spending on AI infrastructure will deliver adequate returns. Analysts have warned that the AI boom may be entering a phase where companies are judged not just on their growth potential but also on the cost of building and operating their infrastructure. “The market’s moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI,” said Ted Parkhill, founder and CEO of Incline Investment Management as quoted by the news agency.You use AI every day. articles.title: As California’s billionaire tax faces defeat, problems for wealthy tech execs may not be over
articles.summary: California’s ultra-wealthy tech executives appear on the verge of defeating a state wealth tax, but their tax battles are far from finished.
articles.body: California’s ultra-wealthy tech executives appear on the verge of defeating a state wealth tax, but their tax battles are far from finished. While election officials continue counting ballots, early returns show 56% of California voters rejecting Proposition 40, compared to 44% in favour. As the ballot measure requires a simple majority to pass, election analysts say defeat is virtually assured, as per a report by CNBC. The measure sought to impose a one-time 5% levy on the net worth of California residents holding more than $1 billion in assets.While Silicon Valley billionaires breathe a sigh of relief at home, tax experts warn that the state-level fight could catalyse a much broader push in Washington, where newly empowered Democrats in Congress are eyeing federal tax increases on top earners and a potential federal wealth tax, the report added.Countermeasures seal Prop 40’s fateThe billionaire tax ran into direct opposition from two competing ballot measures designed as legislative countermeasures.Proposition 41: Restricts how state tax revenue can be spent.Proposition 42: Explicitly prohibits the state from taxing personal assets.Both countermeasures are currently winning majority support among voters. Under California election rules, if either proposition receives more total votes than Proposition 40, the billionaire tax is officially nullified, the report added.Faced with the mounting deficit, the proposal’s primary backer conceded defeat with the healthcare union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW West) announcing plans to reintroduce the initiative in 2028 unless state lawmakers intervene to “make billionaires pay their fair share.”Mixed results for wealth taxes across other US statesWhile California voters rejected taxing accumulated net worth, measures aimed at taxing high-income earners saw stronger momentum elsewhere. In Washington State, voters approved a new “millionaire tax,” establishing a 9.9% tax rate on household income exceeding $1 million per year.In Colorado, a ballot measure seeking to replace the state’s 4.4% flat tax with a graduated income tax, featuring an 8.4% top bracket on earnings above $1 million, remains too close to call.Federal scrutiny awaits in Democrat controlled CongressWith Democrats now positioned to take control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, tax policy analysts anticipate a wave of federal legislation designed to increase levies on wealthy individuals and corporations to fund middle-class relief.“It is clear Democrats will try to lower taxes for middle-income households and raise taxes on certain businesses and high-income households. But it is much too soon to know how,” said Howard Gleckman, nonresident fellow at the Tax Policy Center, as per CNBC.Federal lawmakers could revive legislative frameworks introduced during the last congressional cycle by Democratic Senators Chris Van Hollen of Maryland and Cory Booker of New Jersey. Van Hollen’s proposal introduces a graduated surtax on incomes surpassing $1 million:$1 Million to $2 Million: A 5% surtax.Over $5 Million: A 12% surtax.Top Marginal Income Rate: Would rise to 49%, up from the current 37% federal ceiling.Capital Gains: The top long-term capital gains tax rate would jump from 23.8% to 35.8%.To counterbalance the tax hikes, the plan proposes expanding exemptions for middle- and lower-income filers, creating a $46,000 deduction for single tax filers and a $92,000 deduction for joint filers.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pope Leo begins major Latin America tour three weeks after lung surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to embark on an extensive tour of Latin America, just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV is set to embark on an extensive tour of Latin America, just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The 12-day visit will include a much-awaited return to Peru, where he spent several years serving as a priest.The Vatican has maintained that no special medical arrangements have been made for the trip, describing the pontiff as a “71-year-old who has undergone an operation” rather than someone living with a “permanent medical condition”.Pope Leo disclosed last month that doctors had detected a tumour during a routine medical scan. Surgeons removed the growth along with the lower lobe of his right lung, with his medical team subsequently confirming that the cancer had not spread.According to the BBC report, speaking to reporters in Rome ahead of the visit, which will cover Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, a Vatican spokeswoman said the Pope had “fantastic stamina” and was “extremely enthusiastic” about the programme. She added that he had personally approved the entire schedule without making any changes.Back on trackProfessor Massimo Faggioli of Villanova university that the Vatican was using the visit to signal that the Pope's health setback had been temporary and that he had resumed his regular responsibilities.“The Vatican's message with this trip is, 'that was a short episode and now we're back on track',” he said, noting that Leo had returned to a demanding schedule of speeches and public audiences following his surgery.The professor added that the Pope appeared to be in good health, with his recent public engagements reinforcing that impression.However, the 12-day tour is expected to be physically demanding, involving several long-distance and domestic flights and covering thousands of miles across diverse landscapes, from the Amazon rainforest to the Andes.Uruguay will be the first stop. The country has witnessed a significant decline in its Catholic population in recent years and is set to welcome a Pope for the first time in 40 years.From there, Leo will travel to Argentina, the birthplace of his predecessor, Pope Francis.Father Fernando Laguna, rector of Santa Maria Addolorata, Argentina's national church in Rome, described the visit as a tribute to Francis, who never travelled to his homeland as pontiff.He told the BBC that the announcement had brought immense happiness to the Argentine community and said he had always believed Leo would make the journey despite his health condition.To enable parishioners to follow the visit, the priest is arranging a large screen inside the Rome church. The building has also been decorated with posters welcoming the pontiff, including one that reads, “We're waiting for you!”The Argentina leg, featuring meetings with political leaders and religious engagements, could prove to be the most politically sensitive part of the tour.President Javier Milei had previously attacked Pope Francis, describing him as “evil on earth” and a “communist” over his advocacy of social justice and support for the poor. Argentina's Catholic bishops, meanwhile, have criticised Milei's stringent austerity policies and extensive reductions in social welfare spending.Despite the earlier tensions, Milei has already extended a warm welcome to Pope Leo. In a post on X, the Argentine president said the country was awaiting his arrival with “immense joy”. Millions of people are expected to gather to welcome the pontiff.'Homecoming' to PeruThe final leg of the tour, in Peru, is expected to be its most significant, with the Vatican describing it as a return to the Pope's roots.“He knows these streets,” a Vatican spokeswoman said.Although born in the United States, Leo, formerly known as Robert Prevost, spent nearly two decades in Peru at different stages of his life. He also holds Peruvian citizenship. His experiences in the country are widely regarded as having played an important role in shaping his approach to the papacy.His itinerary includes a visit to the diocese of Chiclayo, where he was ordained bishop in 2014 and served until Pope Francis brought him to the Vatican nearly a decade later.The pontiff will also travel to Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire, where he is scheduled to celebrate Mass at an altitude of more than 3,000 metres. His journey will then take him to Pucallpa in the Amazon region.During the visits to all three countries, the Pope is also expected to meet survivors of clerical sexual abuse. The issue had cast a shadow over Pope Francis's 2018 visit to Chile and Peru.Professor Faggioli described the tour as an opportunity for the papacy to rebuild and strengthen its relationship with Latin America following Francis's sometimes challenging engagements with the region.He also believes Leo has a strong understanding of the Americas as a unified continent, giving him an opportunity to address wider political and social concerns.With democratic institutions facing growing challenges across the region, the professor said there were several important issues the pontiff could raise during his journey.Another major question concerns a possible visit to the United States. Faggioli believes Leo is keen to travel there, although the timing could depend on the political situation and whether Donald Trump remains president.He said the Vatican was likely considering the implications of such a visit.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran security chief meets Putin with Khamenei's letter specifying 7 conditions for US talks
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Moscow on Thursday as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Moscow on Thursday as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran gather pace, with Tehran seeking Moscow’s support on regional security and post-war arrangements.During the meeting, Khamenei aide Rezaei also handed Putin a letter from Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, Iranian state broadcaster Press TV reported, according to Al Jazeera.The meeting came at a time when US President Donald Trump is facing a major political setback after Republicans lost control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections. The results have weakened Trump’s political position at home as his administration faces mounting pressure over the economic fallout of the war.Speaking after his meeting with Putin, Rezaei said the discussions focused on regional security arrangements and Russia’s support for ending what he described as US “aggression” against Iran.“Important regional issues were discussed with Putin and significant conversations took place regarding the post-war period and regional security arrangements,” he said.The two sides also discussed expanding energy cooperation, including plans to build gas pipelines connecting Russia and Iran.Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s supreme national Security Council, said Khamenei had instructed him to deliver the letter to Putin as soon as possible. He said the Moscow visit had been planned nearly a month earlier but was postponed due to “daily discussions about the military situation in the region”.He did not disclose the contents of the letter.In a written statement on Wednesday, Khamenei said there should not be “even the slightest inclination towards submission” to the US. He also called for an “ever stronger” Iran to reach a “point of absolute deterrence”.Seven conditions for talksRezaei’s Moscow visit comes amid intensified diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with Qatar also stepping up its efforts to broker a resolution. Concerns have grown that Washington could resume attacks on Iran following the US midterm elections.Trump’s Republican Party lost control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s vote amid widespread anger over rising prices, with many voters blaming the economic fallout on the war with Iran, Al Jazeera reported.The key sticking points in efforts to end the conflict include the future of the strategically important Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports, sanctions on Tehran and the resumption of negotiations over Iran’s nuclear programme.However, Rezaei ruled out negotiations with Washington on ending the war or reopening the Strait of Hormuz until the US meets Tehran’s seven demands.“On the issue of diplomacy, we have announced seven conditions to the Americans. As long as they do not execute our seven conditions, we will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor have negotiations,” he said.Rezaei said Putin had reiterated Moscow’s readiness to help bring the conflict to an end. Last month, Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Russia was prepared to “do everything” it could to support efforts towards that goal, Russian news agencies reported.The Kremlin discussions also covered plans for a gas pipeline linking Russia and Iran. The proposed project is aimed at helping address Iran’s gas shortages while allowing Moscow to supply gas to countries neighbouring Iran.Rezaei further briefed Putin on a meeting held in Tehran in late October involving Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan. He said the Russian president had welcomed the initiative.“Like our Chinese friends, we believe that there should be regional arrangements and that foreign countries should not interfere in the security of the region,” he said.The Kremlin did not immediately issue its own account of the meeting, which was held at the Senate Palace, Russia’s TASS news agency reported.Separately, Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi held telephone conversations with his counterparts in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Turkiye and Jordan.The discussions focused on regional developments and ongoing diplomatic efforts to promote peace, Iranian state media reported.Russia and Iran, both facing extensive Western sanctions, have strengthened their diplomatic and military ties in recent years.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Utah rancher learned of a 3-million-square-foot data center across from his home when a gas company sought a pipeline easement; now he is appealing its permit
articles.summary: A Utah rancher discovers a massive 3-million-square-foot data center planned near his home and is appealing its permit after community concerns arise over lack of notice and environmental impact.
articles.body: Most people would probably expect a heads-up before something huge is built across the road from their home. However, Taylor Flake, a rancher near Mona, Utah, didn't get one. He told The Salt Lake Tribune he had no idea about the project until a gas company representative stopped by his home in August. The representative wanted an easement to run a pipeline through his land. The pipeline would feed a planned data centre campus on 361 acres of farmland across his ranch. The campus would be roughly 3 million square feet, and Flake's group has now appealed the permit.A four-minute hearing and a $10 billion plan The permit came from the Juab County Planning Commission in April. As per The Tribune, the public hearing lasted only 4 minutes, and there were no objections to the project. The planning commission sent a notice about the meeting two weeks earlier, but neighbours say it went under the radar. Flake says that the meeting minutes were not made available to the public until late August. The permit application revealed that the Nebo North LLC campus could have up to 10 buildings, each around 300,000 square feet. That's about 3 million square feet, all together roughly the size of 20 Costco stores. The Tribune says it's a $10 billion project.What the neighbours are asking for Flake’s group appealed on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, a week after more than 100 people jammed a county commission meeting. It's called Mona Cares: neighbours for responsible development. It asks the county to overturn the permit decision and start the approval process over again with “adequate and actual notice” to residents. It also asks for a process that protects the residents’ rights to seek a referendum. It wants the project work to be halted pending appeal. Neighbours argue that the campus should not be allowed under agricultural zones. Construction would mean traffic, dust and debris on Goshen Canyon Road. When it's up and running, the data centre could create noise, light and air pollution, residents say.How a conditional use permit works Conditional Uses, a training presentation by the Utah office of the property rights Ombudsman, explains how this type of permit usually works. According to the state agency, the permit is normally an administrative process. This means that authorities apply pre-existing laws to determine the issue of a particular case rather than create new legislation. The agency says officials must approve a conditional use if reasonable conditions can reduce its expected harms under local standards. Moreover, they can gather facts from residents but can't rely on public opinion or preferences. The community demanded that the county review the issuance of this permit.Why data centers raise bigger questionsLawrence Berkeley National Laboratory estimated in its 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report that US data centres consumed about 176 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2023. That was 4.4 percent of national electricity consumption. The report predicted a range of 325 to 580 terawatt-hours by 2028, or about 6.7 percent to 12 percent of US power. These are national estimates. They don't mention anything specific about the Mona project. But they may help explain growing concern about proposals like this one.What happens next As of mid-September reporting, the county had not said if it would accept the appeal. County Commissioner Clinton Painter had said the county followed state law when it processed the permit. But commissioners also indicated they weren't sure if they had the authority to overturn the April decision. The county clerk’s office told The Tribune that the county attorney had counselled officials not to comment. Flake wanted people to be heard before decisions like this disrupt their lives. Whatever the outcome, the case shows how much clear notice actually matters.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Hawaii’s USS Arizona is still leaking oil more than 80 years after Pearl Harbour; researchers found its chemical makeup varies by leak point, with an estimated 600,000 gallons still aboard
articles.summary: A recent study reveals that the USS Arizona continues to leak oil more than 80 years after its sinking, with unique chemical compositions at various leak points and an estimated 600,000 gallons of oil remaining onboard. This research prompts critical considerations for managing other WWII shipwrecks.
articles.body: Some scars from the Second World War simply refuse to disappear. The USS Arizona, which sank at Pearl Harbour, Hawaii, still leaks oil 80 years later, according to the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. Research from the institution and the University of Houston led to a new study in Marine Pollution Bulletin that analysed oil samples from several leak points on the wreck. They found that the oil isn't the same in all places. The work also has lessons for thousands of other Second World War wrecks around the globe.Why this wreck is so tricky The Arizona isn't just another shipwreck. It is also a war grave and a memorial site, so any work there needs to be done with care and respect. David Conlin, a marine archaeologist with the National Park Service, noted that this particular site requires nothing less than the best and most careful science possible. The scientist also emphasised that the research team took a respectful and non-intrusive approach to collecting data. Researchers believe that 600,000 gallons of oil still remain on the ship. That's a lot of oil to have sitting in one place for over eight decades. The good thing about the situation is that the oil is not leaking at a highly concerning rate, according to Chris Reddy, a marine chemist at Woods Hole and one of the authors of the study. Yet the research emphasises the need for ongoing monitoring and preparedness at the site.What the oil samples showedThe team analysed oil collected by the National Park Service in 2016 and 2018. They used advanced molecular fingerprinting, which maps the composition of an oil and where it likely came from. Testing showed it was a heavy fuel oil refined from California crude. This is the type of fuel the US Navy used to fuel its ships in the early 1940s. The oil still has high levels of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These compounds are known to be long-lived and can be toxic. However, Reddy noted that not all of the PAHs found here are highly toxic.Why every leak has its own fingerprint The oil was initially the same fuel, but its chemistry changes depending on leaks. According to Jagoš Radović, the lead author of the University of Houston paper, the oil changes even before it leaves the vessel. While moving through the network of wreckage, it comes across different oxygen content, water flow, and microbes that create a unique chemical signature for each leak. Natural weathering is also a big factor, with microbes breaking the oil down and some of it dissolving in water. Lighter compounds gradually disappear while the biomarkers stay intact. This allows scientists to trace where the oil came from and how it changes over time. The Marine Pollution Bulletin study described the oil as chemically complex after more than 75 years underwater at the time of sampling in 2016 and 2018.What it means for other shipwrecksThe Arizona is not alone. The ocean floor is littered with thousands of wrecks from World War II, holding millions of gallons of unrecovered fuel. Many are sitting near the shore. The Arizona is giving scientists a rare chance to watch over decades how oil behaves in low-oxygen water, which may inform plans for future spills. Reddy said the decision to remove oil is a balance of the risk of a spill and the risk of disturbing the wreck. The amount of oil remaining, the rate of leakage, the local ecosystem and the wreck's historical significance all matter. Sometimes, he said, it is better to watch closely than to step in. The same paper also noted that war graves should not be disturbed by aggressive or intrusive means.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Greenpeace placed boulders weighing up to 2 tonnes on England’s North Sea seabed; it says the barrier blocks bottom trawling across 116 sq km
articles.summary: Greenpeace UK has placed boulders on the North Sea seabed to stop bottom trawling across 116 sq km, aiming to protect harbour porpoises. This action follows the release of Blue Planet III and highlights the need for stricter fishing regulations in marine protected areas.
articles.body: Imagine dropping giant rocks into the sea to keep fishing boats out. That's what Greenpeace UK says it has done. On 2 November, 2026, the group said in a press release that its activists placed boulders weighing up to two tonnes on the seabed of the Southern North Sea off England's east coast. Greenpeace says the barrier prevents bottom trawling, a fishing practice that drags gear across the sea floor, from accessing 116 square kilometres. The area was designated to protect harbour porpoises. Greenpeace calls it the most heavily bottom-trawled offshore protected area in the UK.Why boulders and why nowThe group linked the move to the first episode of Blue Planet III, aired on BBC One the night before the announcement. Greenpeace says it had warned back in June that it would take direct action if the government failed to act, and nothing had been done yet. The group itself has declared the area an ‘Ocean Park,’ a campaign label, and said its ship, the Arctic Sunrise, will be patrolling the zone in the coming days to deter other destructive fishing activities. Simon Pegg and Benedict Cumberbatch signed their names on the boulders, as did MPs including Kerry McCarthy and Dr Roz Savage.What Greenpeace says is wrong with bottom trawling Greenpeace says bottom trawling can destroy delicate seafloor habitats. It can also leave porpoises hungry by taking away key fish stocks, while intense noise disrupts their hunting. These points are taken from a 2026 report by campaign group Oceana. Despite the site's protected status, the organisation says there are currently no restrictions on fishing activity in most parts of the site. This makes bottom trawlers and other industrial vessels a daily threat to porpoises.What the official body says about the site The Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC) is a public body that advises UK governments on nature-related matters. JNCC notes that the Southern North Sea site spans 36,951 square kilometres. At the time of its designation in 2019, it was the largest special area of conservation in the UK and European waters. The JNCC also states that the site provides a habitat for about 17.5% of the UK’s North Sea harbour porpoise population. Its goals include no significant disturbance to porpoises and leaving their prey available. The 116 square kilometres that Greenpeace says it has effectively closed off is only about 0.3 percent of the total site.The numbers behind the claimGreenpeace analysed data from Global Fishing Watch and found that there are at least 37,200 hours of bottom-towed fishing in the site in 2025. This was far more than any other offshore protected area in the UK. It says that bottom trawlers and dredgers covered a cumulative 55,600 square kilometres of seabed inside the UK’s Marine Protected Areas in 2025. That’s about 58 times the size of Dartmoor National Park. This figure counts every pass of the gear, so it measures the total amount of trawling, not the area trawled. Greenpeace also notes that in 2025, the vessels spent at least 115,000 hours towing gear in those areas. That's equivalent to more than 13 years of non-stop fishing.Government plans and the bigger goal Will McCallum, co-executive director of Greenpeace UK, wants a ban on destructive fishing in all UK protected waters. Greenpeace says only 11 percent of the UK’s marine protected areas (43 out of 378) are fully protected by law from bottom trawling. It also notes that a government plan to outlaw the practice in parts of a further 42 areas, announced in 2025, is still undecided, more than a year after its consultation closed. The Southern North Sea is due in a later round, with no date specified yet. The release contains no government response. The UK has signed up to protect 30% of land and sea for nature by 2030. Greenpeace says just 3.5% of the world's oceans and just 1% of UK waters are fully or highly protected.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: After spending 27 years in prison, a woman inspired a North Carolina farm to build 7 tiny homes where formerly incarcerated women and gender-expansive people can practise living independently
articles.summary: A woman who spent 27 years in prison inspired a North Carolina farm to create seven tiny homes for formerly incarcerated women and gender-expansive people.
articles.body: A woman who spent 27 years in prison inspired a North Carolina farm to create seven tiny homes for formerly incarcerated women and gender-expansive people. In 2019, Deb, a former Benevolence Farm resident, proposed a place where people leaving the shared farmhouse could practise independent living alongside supportive neighbours.The organisation is building the homes on its property in Graham, giving residents individual spaces and a community around them with supportive peers. According to Benevolence Farm, the project aims to help residents manage a household and rebuild their lives after incarceration, with support from peers. The idea came from Deb, and dozens of alumni helped co-design the project.How a woman who spent 27 years in prison inspired the projectDeb approached Benevolence Farm in 2019, after spending 27 years in prison. She had been living in the organisation’s shared farmhouse and valued that experience. However, she was afraid of a neighborhood that did not welcome her. She proposed a place where she could practise living independently while still having supportive neighbours nearby.According to Benevolence Farm, her request became the starting point for the Tiny Home Community. Dozens of the farm’s alumni have helped co-design the project. The organisation says the homes will let residents practise managing a single household while having supportive peers nearby. The idea is to make independent living possible without leaving residents isolated from a community they can rely on for support.Seven individual homes designed for independent livingThe development would include seven individual homes on Benevolence Farm’s property in Graham, North Carolina. The organisation describes it as a first-of-its-kind tiny home community created for and by formerly incarcerated women and gender-expansive people. Each resident will have a private home rather than living in a shared group setting. The community is intended to help residents practise independent living while remaining part of a supportive network.The farm described the homes as an alternative to traditional congregate reentry housing, which it said often replicates conditions and trauma associated with incarceration.The homes are being designed around trauma-informed principles, with private, dignified living space for residents as they work towards rebuilding their lives after prison.North Carolina farm receives $1.1 million towards housing projectNorth Carolina First Lady Anna Stein delivered keynote remarks at the ceremony, which brought together state housing officials, community leaders, farm alumni and supporters. Representatives of the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency also attended. The agency contributed $1.1 million towards the development, according to its chair, Adam Abram.The farm put the total cost of completing the project at $1,792,202. This amount includes architectural design, engineering, site preparation, construction, landscaping, and furnishing.Mona Evans, the farm’s Community Advocacy Director, and Linda Cayton, a farm alumna and local Certified Peer Support Specialist, spoke at the event about the importance of independent housing for successful reentry after prison.Tiny home community expected to open in fall/winter 2026According to the farm, the community was under construction and was scheduled to open in fall/winter 2026. Its project timeline lists a ribbon-cutting ceremony for November 12, 2026, when the homes are also due to open for public tours. Residents are expected to receive their keys and move in during fall/winter 2026. Benevolence Farm says residents will be able to practise managing a single household while living among supportive peers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: After 22-day protest, Parvinder Singh Jhota's family agrees to post-mortem, body shifted to PGIMER Chandigarh
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: The body of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota was brought to PGIMER in Chandigarh from Mansa on Friday for a post-mortem, after
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: The body of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota was brought to PGIMER in Chandigarh from Mansa on Friday for a post-mortem, after his family agreed to the procedure and called off their 22-day-long agitation following talks with Punjab government representatives.The body, which had been kept at the mortuary of the civil hospital in Mansa for more than three weeks, was shifted to PGIMER in an ambulance late Thursday night.Jhota was shot dead inside a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa on October 13.His father, Bhim Singh, told reporters at PGIMER on Friday that the family would return to Mansa with the body after the post-mortem. He said the last rites would be performed on Friday or Saturday, depending on the time they reach Mansa.A joint action committee seeking justice for Jhota had been demanding, among other things, the release of two of its arrested members, including Lakhvir Singh alias Lakha Sidhana. The arrested members were released from Nabha district jail on Thursday evening.The breakthrough came on Wednesday after a five-hour meeting involving Jhota's family, the joint action committee and Punjab government representatives, including Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian, following a three-week-long deadlock.After the meeting, the state government agreed to release the arrested protesters and withdraw the cases registered against them. It also assured Rs 2 crore in compensation to Jhota's family and a government job for his wife.On Thursday night, Jhota's body was transported from the civil hospital in Mansa to Chandigarh in an ambulance.According to the case details, medical store owner Ashwani Kumar opened fire at Jhota on October 13 after the latter questioned him for allegedly selling addictive drugs to an elderly man. Kumar was arrested from Salasar in Rajasthan.The incident, which took place while Jhota was hosting a Facebook Live session, triggered a political slugfest in Punjab, which is scheduled to go to polls early next year.Several political leaders, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Congress leader Sachin Pilot, Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal and Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon, had met Jhota's family.Following the murder, opposition parties stepped up their attack on the Bhagwant Mann-led government over drug-related issues and the law and order situation in the state.The joint action committee, comprising various organisations and social activists, had also been demanding the resignations of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and Punjab Police DGP Gaurav Yadav.Agriculture Minister Khudian visited Jhota's family on Tuesday evening, becoming the first AAP leader to meet the bereaved family.Earlier, the Punjab government had handed over the investigation into Jhota's death to the CBI following a demand by his family. The government had also suspended an SHO, a DSP and a drug inspector in connection with the case.The government also agreed to the family's demands for setting up a trauma centre in Jhota's memory and providing compensation to each of the four people injured in the incident.Other demands accepted by the government include the installation of a statue of Jhota at a suitable location in Mansa.(With Agency Inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: During World War II, U.S. Navy sailor Vernon Shaw mailed Evelyn Holland an engagement ring; after more than 60 years of marriage, she and their daughter donated his letters and uniform to a Navy museum
articles.summary: Discover the touching story of WWII sailor Vernon Shaw, who mailed an engagement ring to his love, Evelyn Holland. Their correspondence and over 60 years of marriage culminated in a heartfelt donation to the Navy museum, preserving their wartime romance for future generations.
articles.body: Thousands of American service members were deployed far away from home during the Second World War. Handwritten letters became an important method of communication with loved ones. For US Navy sailor Vernon Shaw, a letter to his wife, Evelyn Holland, was not only a form of contact but also a symbol of hope and love that would help to sustain a relationship and give hope of reunion for several years spent apart.While stationed in the Pacific, he sent Evelyn an engagement ring with a letter announcing his intention to marry her, hoping that she would be by his side when the war ended. The couple married and remained together for more than 60 years. Subsequently, Holland and their daughter donated his Navy uniform and wartime letters to the naval museum so that other people could learn about the love and commitment during World War 2.Nearly 200 letters kept their relationship aliveAccording to the US Naval History and Heritage Command, Shaw was an aviation machinist's mate, third class, in the US Navy and spent much of the war period aboard the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise (CV-6). The ship operated in the Pacific in the main theatres of war against Japan, and his military service kept him at sea for long periods. Keeping in touch with Holland was a significant aspect of their relationship. The letters they exchanged, which ultimately numbered close to 200, were written from the naval bases in the US, Hawaii, and on the carrier.An early letter of Shaw's was notable for its story-like tone. He depicts a young couple in love, where a schoolboy filled with precocity and nerve who asked a girl out on a date. It's set against the backdrop of the war and the threatening spark of their affection. He sent Holland an engagement ring in the post, so he'd have a ready-made future to come back to. Their letter writing was typical of the wartime experience, an essential means for men and women separated by the war to keep alive their longing for each other.A wartime reunion led to marriageShaw was back in the United States in 1945 for an extended period after many years of war. His 30-day leave was the time when he and his beloved married on 16th January 1945. Shaw and Holland tied the knot at the First Baptist Church in Fernandina, Florida. Shaw wore his Navy service dress uniform, as a reminder of the service that had brought them together.They were married for over 60 years after the war that had kept them apart ended. Their letters, which bridged the distance between them, soon became a family heirloom, preserving their courtship and wartime separation. Wartime correspondence took on special meaning for the families of American soldiers and sailors. The National Postal Museum documents how the U.S. military introduced V-Mail during the Second World War to make transporting letters more efficient. The system photographed written messages onto microfilm, reducing the space required for military mail.Family donation preserved the sailor's personal historyMore than 60 years after the wedding, Holland and their daughter Jill decided to tell Shaw's wartime story by donating some of his belongings to the National Naval Aviation Museum. In 2012, they sent the Navy uniform, which showed what he wore during the war, along with the first letter he had written to Holland, to the museum. The donation allowed the Museum to preserve items connected to his service career as well as his marriage. The uniform was a tangible reminder of his Navy service, but the letters told the story of the young sailor behind the uniform and how they were able to maintain the marriage despite the time and distance between the couple.The story was later written up by the Museum in its objects of history series as Enterprise Sailor Tells a Love Story. It uncovered an item that otherwise could have been left in the family. Shaw and Holland's correspondence shows how individual exchanges can serve as valuable historical documents, capturing the hopes and uncertainties of a wartime romance, and how that history can be linked to a larger national narrative.You use AI every day. articles.title: English singer Adele once said her £5.99 million West Sussex mansion gave her the creeps; 14 years later, its owner claims her comments are still driving buyers away
articles.summary: Adele's former home, a £5.99 million Grade II-listed mansion in West Sussex, has reportedly struggled to find a buyer after the singer described parts of
articles.body: Adele's former home, a £5.99 million Grade II-listed mansion in West Sussex, has reportedly struggled to find a buyer after the singer described parts of it as frightening during a 2012 television interview. The owner of Lock House in Partridge Green claims that her comments about the ten-bedroom property being haunted damaged its reputation and affected attempts to sell it. According to a planning application reported by the BBC, the owner has tried to sell the mansion for around 14 years. The property is now the subject of proposals to create three residential units and a separate cottage.How did Adele's comments give her former mansion a creepy reputationAccording to the BBC, Adele rented Lock House in Partridge Green, West Sussex, in 2012. The property, which was once a convent, has ten bedrooms and is classified as a Grade II-listed building.During an interview with Anderson Cooper on CBS, the singer spoke about her experience of living in the mansion. Describing one section of the house, she said: "This bit's all quite scary, really."She also explained that she did not like being alone in the property, adding: "I'm not rattling around here on my own. It gives me the creeps."Although Adele described the house as frightening, she did not actually use the word "haunted" during the interview. However, according to the property's owner, her remarks contributed to the mansion developing a reputation that has affected its sale prospects.Adele's haunted mansion comments affect the £5.99 million property's saleIn a planning application submitted to Horsham District Council, the owner claimed that Adele's comments had made marketing the property more difficult. The application stated: "The first tenant, Adele, stayed for six months and blighted the property by saying it is haunted."It also said: "This comment negatively impacted future marketing efforts and continues to affect the property's reputation to this day."According to the application, the owner has actively attempted to sell Lock House for approximately 14 years. The property was put back on the market after Adele left, but reportedly attracted no offers.The owner also claimed that the only offer received came in August 2020. However, the prospective buyer withdrew after learning about the property's supposed haunted reputation.What happened to Adele's former £5.99 million mansion after she moved outFollowing Adele's departure, Lock House was relisted for sale. It was subsequently rented to a tenant who intended to operate a bespoke dressmaking business from the property.However, according to the planning application, the owner later discovered that the tenant was operating a residential retreat with 11 guest bedrooms and a fitness boot camp.The property has also been the subject of proposals to change its use. The owner submitted a planning application seeking permission to transform the mansion from a single dwelling into three residential units. The proposal also included converting an existing garage and flat into a separate cottage.What makes Adele's former £5.99 million mansion a luxurious 32-acre estateLock House was originally built around 1909 and underwent a major reconstruction programme in 1940. In 1971, the property was divided into 26 separate lots and sold at auction.It was subsequently purchased by the church and became the Convent of the Visitation. The current owner acquired the property in 2003 from a property trader who had previously purchased it after the convent relocated to Albourne.The mansion and its surrounding 32-acre estate include ten bedrooms, ten bathrooms, indoor and outdoor swimming pools, a tennis court, a helicopter pad and a cinema room.According to its listing at the time of the BBC report, Lock House was being offered for sale at £5,995,000.The owner's planning application highlights the difficulties they claim to have experienced in selling the historic property, with Adele's comments about feeling frightened inside the mansion continuing to feature in its marketing history.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: How Bengaluru family was massacred inside house on 59th Cross: 2 days, a party invitation, chemicals to erase bloodstains
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A party invitation, a grinding stone and chemicals allegedly used to clean up bloodstains — a cab driver in Bengaluru is accused of murdering
articles.body: BENGALURU: A party invitation, a grinding stone and chemicals allegedly used to clean up bloodstains — a cab driver in Bengaluru is accused of murdering seven members of his wife's family, including a seven-year-old boy, over a domestic dispute.The accused, identified as Indushekar, allegedly first murdered his wife, Sunita, before killing six members of her family over the next two days at his house, police sources said on Friday.He allegedly disposed of the bodies at different locations in Bengaluru and neighbouring districts, including Chikkaballapur.The victims have been identified as Sunita; her mother, Roopavati; her brothers, Shivakumar and Shankar; their wives, both named Divya; and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth.Police have so far recovered Puneeth's body, while efforts are under way to trace the remaining bodies.The couple had been married for about 20 years and frequently argued over Sunita's visits to her parental home, according to preliminary findings. Attempts by family members to reconcile them failed to resolve their differences.Indushekar allegedly resented the support Sunita received from her mother and brothers. Police suspect that the domestic dispute may have been the motive behind the killings.How events unfoldedAccording to police sources, Indushekar first allegedly murdered Sunita using a grinding stone at their house on 59th Cross, near Bahsyam Circle.He wrapped her body in cloth and allegedly dumped it near Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur district. He subsequently switched off her mobile phone and told neighbours that she had gone on a trip, allegedly to avoid suspicion.The following day, Indushekar allegedly invited his brothers-in-law, Shivakumar and Shankar, to his house for a party and killed them using the grinding stone.He subsequently allegedly murdered their wives, both named Divya, his mother-in-law, Roopavati, and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth, police sources said.The alleged multiple murders came to light after a missing-person complaint was lodged at Srirampura police station on Thursday.During the investigation, police uncovered evidence pointing to the killings and arrested Indushekar. Investigators are questioning him to establish the exact sequence of events and where he disposed of the bodies.Chemicals allegedly used to clean houseAfter the killings, Indushekar allegedly used chemicals to clean the house and remove bloodstains, according to police sources.Police have seized the grinding stone allegedly used in the murders and the car suspected to have been used to transport the bodies.Puneeth's body was recovered following an extensive search near Nandi Hills. Police are continuing efforts to locate the remaining bodies, which are suspected to have been dumped at different locations, including Charmadi Ghat in coastal Karnataka.During questioning, Indushekar reportedly told police that he was distressed over domestic disputes.Investigators are also examining whether anyone assisted him in carrying out the murders, including the possible role of his daughter. Police are yet to establish whether he acted alone.Another aspect of the investigation is how the killings went unnoticed despite the house being situated in a residential neighbourhood.Police are continuing their investigation to establish the exact timeline of the murders, the circumstances surrounding each killing and the locations where the remaining bodies were disposed of.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: In 2021, Shaquille O'Neal's foundation helped turn a former Georgia middle school into a youth club with a $1.1 million renovation; within a year, the new centre had more than 400 registered children and teens
articles.summary: In 2021, Shaquille O’Neal’s foundation helped transform a former Georgia middle school into a Boys and Girls Club designed to give local children and
articles.body: In 2021, Shaquille O’Neal’s foundation helped transform a former Georgia middle school into a Boys and Girls Club designed to give local children and teenagers a safe place to learn, create and grow. The Shaquille O’Neal Boys and Girls Club of Henry County opened in August after a $1.1 million renovation of the former Henry County Middle School, according to The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation. Within its first year, the centre had registered more than 400 young members, turning an unused school building into a busy community hub for Henry County families.The project was more than a celebrity donation. It grew out of a three-year community engagement effort led by a local advisory board, with support from Boys and Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta, the City of McDonough, Henry County, the Henry County Board of Education and other partners. For O’Neal, the cause was personal: he said the Boys and Girls Club had provided a safe space for him while he was growing up and helped shape who he became.A former school finds a new purposeThe club occupies the former Henry County Middle School, a building that was given a $1.1 million renovation before it opened to local children and teenagers. Rather than demolishing or leaving the property idle, the project repurposed the space into facilities designed for education, recreation and creative development.The renovated centre includes a learning centre, computer lab, arts and crafts centre, music studio, game room, multipurpose room, outdoor garden and gym. That mix reflects the broader Boys and Girls Club approach, which combines academic support with activities that encourage confidence, teamwork and healthy habits.For families in Henry County, the opening filled an important gap. Boys and Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta said the club was launched as a community response to a critical need at a crucial time, providing a safe, inclusive and engaging environment during the hours when young people may otherwise lack structured support.Shaq’s $1 million commitmentThe Shaquille O’Neal Foundation committed $1 million to the project, with additional support from partners including The Papa John’s Foundation for Building Community. Those resources helped make the renovation and opening possible, alongside contributions from Boys and Girls Clubs of America and local government and education partners.The foundation, established in 2019 by the NBA Hall of Famer, television sports analyst and entrepreneur, describes its mission as creating pathways for underserved youth and helping them reach their full potential. Its work is primarily focused on partnerships with Boys and Girls Clubs and Communities In Schools in Atlanta and Las Vegas.O’Neal’s connection to the cause gave the project particular visibility. At the club’s first-anniversary celebration in July 2022, he said he was proud to help create similar pathways to success for children in Henry County, echoing the role that a Boys and Girls Club had played in his own life.More than 400 members in one yearThe results came quickly. By the time the club marked its first anniversary, it had more than 400 registered members, according to Boys and Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta and The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation. That level of participation showed that the demand for youth programming in the area was substantial.The anniversary event brought together youth members, parents, community partners and corporate supporters. It began with a musical performance by club members and ended with a special presentation to O’Neal from the Torch Club, a youth leadership group within the Boys and Girls Club movement.David Jernigan, president and chief executive of Boys and Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta, said the club had helped ignite the potential of hundreds of Henry County children and teenagers in its first year. Jim Clark, president and chief executive of Boys and Girls Clubs of America, also praised the project and said the organisation looked forward to expanding its impact for more young people and families.Why safe spaces matterYouth development organisations often focus on the hours outside school, when children and teenagers may be unsupervised or without access to enrichment activities. A club can offer homework help, technology access, sports, arts programming and mentoring in one place, while also giving parents a reliable community resource.The Henry County club’s facilities were designed with that in mind. A computer lab and learning centre support academic work, while the music studio, arts and crafts centre, gym and outdoor garden give young people different ways to explore interests and build relationships.The club is led by Executive Director Jesse Coltrane, Program Director Jamal Jordan and Teen Director Breanna Varner. At the time of the anniversary, registration was open for fall membership, and Boys and Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta placed particular emphasis on reaching teenagers.A wider network of supportThe Henry County club is part of a larger system. Boys and Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta operates 26 clubs across 11 counties in metropolitan Atlanta and has traditionally served nearly 8,000 children and teenagers aged 6 to 18 each year. Its programs focus on academic success, healthy lifestyles, character and leadership.The organisation also runs Camp Kiwanis, a 160-acre outdoor residence camp. Together, these programs aim to provide consistent support during critical non-school hours, especially for young people who may face barriers to after-school activities, tutoring or safe recreational spaces.The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation’s involvement fits into that wider network. In addition to its club partnerships, the foundation supports initiatives such as O’Neal’s annual Shaq-a-Claus holiday event and projects alongside corporate partners.A lasting community investmentThe transformation of the former Henry County Middle School shows how a vacant or repurposed public building can become a lasting community asset. A $1.1 million renovation created more than classrooms and a gym; it created a place where hundreds of young people could find structure, encouragement and opportunity.Within a year, more than 400 children and teenagers had registered at the Shaquille O’Neal Boys and Girls Club of Henry County. For O’Neal, the project reflected a simple idea drawn from his own experience: that a safe, supportive space can change the direction of a young person’s life.You use AI every day.
